changes.layout: viewer is moved to an unobstructed upper stage; the complete Coral DNA control surface is moved below it
changes.mobile: control panel no longer overlays the coral stage; page becomes vertical-scroll workbench
changes.sizeSystem: six display-scale tiers: 0.05 m, 0.25 m, 1 m, 5 m, 15 m, and 31-62 m evidence-bound colossal mode
changes.scaleBridge: tier buttons drive the existing age-scale range input and retain the selected tier in localStorage
changes.evidenceReadout: hard-polyp diameter, soft-coral growth, house-scale massive coral and 2026 colossal Porites boundary are shown in the control dock

evidence.source: NOAA Ocean Service — How do corals grow?
facts: hard coral polyps average about 1-3 mm in diameter
massive corals may range from egg-sized to house-sized
soft coral colonies can grow about 2-4 cm per year
soft corals use flexible support and occur as trees, bushes, fans, whips and grasses

evidence.source: NOAA Ocean Service — Colossal coral in the Mariana Islands, 2026-03-17
facts: reported Porites rus colony was about 31 m across the top and 62 m at the base

evidence.source: Coral Reef Research Foundation — Species Diversity
facts: about 310 stony coral species around Palau main islands plus roughly 20 in southwest islands
reef-building corals decline around 60-75 m on Palau slopes and deep gorgonian/soft-coral communities become important

truthBoundary.sizeTiers: observation and generator-control tiers, not species-specific adult-size claims
truthBoundary.colossalMode: evidence boundary for massive Porites-like reef structures; it must not be applied to all morphology kernels
